stemMarkdown: The price of an article is first increased by 21%, and then the new price is decreased by 19%. What is the net percentage change in price? (Enter a negative value if it is a net decrease.)
solutionMarkdown: Take the original price as 100. After a 21% increase: $100 \times (1 + 21/100) = 121.00$. After a 19% decrease on 121.00: $121.00 \times (1 - 19/100) = 98.01$. Net change $= 98.01 - 100 = -1.99\%$.
altSolutionMarkdown: Shortcut formula: net \% change $= p_1 - p_2 - \dfrac{p_1 p_2}{100} = 21 - 19 - \dfrac{399}{100} = -1.99\%$.
